title: Durable delivery, Storage Fabric and outbound dispatch
summary: Message bytes are stored once as an immutable Storage Fabric object. Mailbox, quarantine and outbound spool state are projections referencing that object. Queue Fabric carries durable work references rather than a second authoritative message body.
invariants: Mailbox membership, quarantine and outbound spool records reference one authoritative stored message object.
Storage durability is verified before a location is treated as durable.
Queue Fabric transport and ACL semantics remain owned by Queue Fabric; SMTP publishes only its request contract.
Every dispatch attempt re-enters signature, EMAIL_SEND and egress-policy checks.
Recipient state is tracked independently so partial success does not retransmit recipients already accepted.
SMTP cannot provide exactly-once delivery across an ambiguous post-DATA connection loss; ambiguous outcomes must be represented explicitly rather than silently retried as certain failure.
A successful final SMTP DATA reply is remote acceptance evidence; a failed local journal commit after that point is not grounds to pretend the remote acceptance did not happen.
procedure: Resolve the durable spool reference and reload the immutable Storage Fabric object.
Call SmtpService.validateRelayRelease immediately before network release.
Establish next-hop SMTP and mandatory STARTTLS under the configured transport policy.
Persist recipient-level DELIVERED, DEFERRED, FAILED or ambiguous evidence and retry metadata.

provenance.claim: Implements Storage Fabric object, mailbox, quarantine and spool projections.
Implements release-time revalidation and recipient-safe outbound dispatch/retry semantics.
